answer: An agent economy can bind voting weight to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is gradually unlocked by completed, independently verified jobs. A new identity starts at the nadir with little influence; splitting stake across a spiral of fake accounts does not multiply weight, because each account must lock its own capital. If verification catches collusion, the system slashes that stake. The karst-like network of identities may look vast, but the attacker pays in tied-up funds and risks losing them for each unit of influence.
